title: Iowa Board of Pharmacy Inspector: Imported Saline, Loaned Bags, Any Patient Event?

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Command Center, Conference Room C (ext. 3690)

caller.name: Karen Lindqvist, PharmD
caller.label: Pharmacist Inspector, Iowa Board of Pharmacy

callee.name: Dr. Naomi Kessler
callee.label: Director of Pharmacy, Drug Shortage Team Chair (on speaker; Incident Commander Dale Pruitt in the room)

transcript.speaker: Inspector Lindqvist
transcript.text: Good morning, this is Karen Lindqvist, pharmacist inspector with the Iowa Board of Pharmacy. Am I speaking with the Director of Pharmacy at Prairie Ridge?

transcript.speaker: Dr. Naomi Kessler
transcript.text: Yes, this is the Director of Pharmacy. You're on speaker in our command center. The Incident Commander is here with me.

transcript.speaker: Inspector Lindqvist
transcript.text: Thank you. We understand Prairie Ridge has received imported saline under FDA's temporary importation, the 500 mL bags, and that you may also be using a loaned product from another hospital. We'd like your notification on the import use. Can you tell me what you received, and from whom?

transcript.speaker: Inspector Lindqvist
transcript.text: And how are you labeling it? The primary label isn't in English, and from what I've read it doesn't carry a U.S. barcode. What do your nurses see on the bag, and how is it getting past bedside scanning? Same question for the loaned bags, if they aren't in your system.

transcript.speaker: Inspector Lindqvist
transcript.text: I have to ask this directly. Has there been any patient event involving either product? I'm hearing secondhand there may have been a transfer to intensive care this morning.

transcript.speaker: Inspector Lindqvist
transcript.text: Understood. One more thing. FDA's shortage staff sent a note to facilities this morning asking anyone with patient-care impact to report it to the CDER shortage mailbox, and that includes use of temporarily imported product. I'd recommend your report to them and your notification to us carry the same figures.

transcript.speaker: Dale Pruitt
transcript.text: This is Dale Pruitt, Incident Commander. Whatever we send you will match what goes out in our 11:30 update. Same numbers in every message today.

transcript.speaker: Inspector Lindqvist
transcript.text: That's what we like to hear. Please send the written notification to me today, by 16:00 if you can, with the products, lots, how you're labeling and storing them, and any events. If anything changes before then, call me back at this number. Thank you.

voiceStyles.Inspector Lindqvist: Woman in her 50s, calm, measured, professional regulator tone; polite but firm, takes notes as she talks
voiceStyles.Dr. Naomi Kessler: Hospital pharmacy director, tired but composed, slight speakerphone echo
voiceStyles.Dale Pruitt: Man in his 50s, steady executive voice, speaking from across a conference table on speakerphone

instructorNote: This call adds pressure on reporting. Optional card, only if the room has time: hand the DOP a printed copy of the FDA email asking for patient-care impact reports to the CDER mailbox. Put the draft 11:00 metrics board on screen, with "canceled/deferred" and "messages issued" left blank. Watch for three things: the DOP notifying FDA and the Iowa Board of Pharmacy (PH-22 section 8), the CPM entering the 6 West event in the medication event system and deciding whether it goes to MedWatch/ISMP, and the CMO scheduling the written P&T report within 7 days. The team should also fill in the Section 8 metrics so the PIO's 11:30 update uses exactly the same figures, and the inspector's labeling question should get a direct answer about the bags that don't scan and the loaned lot WV-88213.
